clue.text: Charitable appeal to an actor

parts.note: a plea to be kind, worded as a plea to a performer to put on a fine act on stage

explanation.walkthrough: The phrase means to help someone kindly, but read literally it asks an actor to give a good performance, a 'turn' being a stage act.
explanation.definitionFit: Helping someone out of kindness is a charitable deed, and a performer's 'turn' is their act on stage.

clue.text: Doctor upset by an expression of scorn in Nebraska

indicators.note: in a down clue, upset means the word is turned over, read from the bottom up

parts.note: MO is Medical Officer, a doctor
aha can be a mocking exclamation

explanation.surface: A doctor in the Midwest is put out by someone's contemptuous remark.
explanation.definitionFit: Omaha is the largest city of the US state of Nebraska, so it is found there.

clue.text: Grain consumer of comparatively large size

parts.note: gr is the standard abbreviation for grain, a small unit of weight
an eater is one who consumes food

explanation.surface: A big bird or animal that feeds on grain is described as relatively large.
explanation.definitionFit: A comparative adjective: bigger in size than something else.

clue.text: Lots of simpletons head off

indicators.note: the first letter of the word for simpletons is cut away

parts.note: noodles is an old word for fools or simpletons

explanation.surface: A great number of fools are moving off somewhere.
explanation.definitionFit: Oodles is informal for a large quantity, a great many.

clue.text: United to win over the lady

parts.note: to get someone is to win them over
her refers to a woman already mentioned

explanation.surface: A suitor is determined to win a woman's heart so they can be united.
explanation.definitionFit: People who are joined as one are united, acting as a single body.

clue.text: Holds out against the weird sisters

indicators.note: weird signals the letters of the next word are put in a strange new order

explanation.surface: Someone stands firm against the three witches of Macbeth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The weird sisters' are Macbeth's witches, so 'weird' looks descriptive but is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: To resist is to withstand or refuse to give in to something.

clue.text: Republican leader gets a mes sage on the grapevine

parts.note: George Bush, Republican president of the United States
a telegraph is a message sent by wire; the print splits the word in two

explanation.surface: A party leader receives a message through gossip.
explanation.walkthrough: A bush telegraph, originally Australian, is the informal passing of news by word of mouth.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are informal networks by which rumour and news spread from person to person.

clue.text: Wild fowl wrapped in absorbent cotton and tissue

indicators.note: the birds are put inside the dressing, which is wrapped around them

parts.note: lint is a soft fabric used for dressing wounds
game means wild birds hunted for sport or food

explanation.surface: A game bird is swaddled in cotton wool as a dressing for its wounds.
explanation.definitionFit: A ligament is a band of fibrous connective tissue joining bones.

clue.text: The last drink for a tramp

definitions.text: The last drink for a tramp

parts.words: The last drink for a tramp
parts.note: a final drink before leaving, pictured as a nip given to a wanderer who will then walk the highway

explanation.walkthrough: The phrase means a final drink before departure; the tramp is the vagrant on the road, so the joke is literal.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom names a final drink taken before setting off home.

clue.text: The custom which is as old as America itself

definitions.text: The custom which is as old as America itself

parts.words: The custom which is as old as America itself
parts.note: a habit long established, joking that the word combines the letters of the country with a word for years elapsed

explanation.walkthrough: Usage is customary practice; the word itself starts with US (America) and ends with AGE, run together.
explanation.definitionFit: Established practice or habit is what a custom is.

clue.text: Dieting so wildly could affect it adversely

definitions.text: Dieting so wildly could affect it adversely

indicators.note: wildly signals the letters of the words before it are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: Crash dieting can upset the stomach.
explanation.definitionFit: Severe dieting can harm the body's process of breaking down food, and the clue's letters make that word.

clue.text: Let father contrive to appear sincere

indicators.note: contrive tells us to engineer the letters into a different order

explanation.surface: A child lets their dad scheme to look genuine.
explanation.definitionFit: Heartfelt feelings are deeply and honestly meant.

clue.text: To students they are the symbol of authority

definitions.text: To students they are the symbol of authority

parts.words: To students they are the symbol of authority
parts.note: teachers in a school are the authority figures for pupils, and a rod carried by an official is an emblem of power

explanation.walkthrough: The word means both the teaching body ('they' to students) and a rod carried as a symbol of office.
explanation.definitionFit: The teachers of a school form its personnel, and a ceremonial rod signifies rank.

clue.text: Attempt to overturn an iron stronghold

indicators.note: overturn means the symbol for the metal is turned backwards

parts.note: Fe is the chemical symbol for iron
a fort is a fortified stronghold

explanation.surface: An attack on a metal-clad castle is mounted.
explanation.definitionFit: An effort is a try, an exertion of strength to achieve something.

clue.text: The point in abstaining from food at the banquet

indicators.note: in places the compass letter inside the word for going without food

parts.note: fasting is going without food
E is east, a point of the compass

explanation.surface: Someone wonders why bother fasting when there's a feast on.
explanation.definitionFit: Those at a banquet are eating lavishly, enjoying a feast.

clue.text: Males curse if they're given any other clothes

parts.note: men are adult males
to swear is to curse

explanation.surface: Men swear if forced into clothes they didn't choose.
explanation.definitionFit: Menswear is clothing designed for men.

clue.text: Every aromatic flavouring? No, only one

definitions.text: Every aromatic flavouring? No, only one

parts.words: Every aromatic flavouring? No, only one
parts.note: the name suggests a blend of all seasonings, yet it is a single berry from one tree

explanation.walkthrough: Allspice is the dried berry of the pimento tree, named because it tastes like a mix of cinnamon, nutmeg and cloves.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a single seasoning whose name suggests every kind of aromatic.

clue.text: Black with age, but it can be cleaned off

parts.note: an era is an age, a long period of time
sable is black in heraldry and poetry

explanation.surface: Something blackened by years can still be wiped clean.
explanation.definitionFit: Something erasable can be rubbed out or wiped away.

clue.text: A refusal by the king to have anyone else

parts.note: no is a refusal
R is short for rex, Latin for king

explanation.surface: The monarch declines to marry someone, preferring another.
explanation.definitionFit: Another means a different one, some other person.

clue.text: Put an end to the production of hard liquor

definitions.meaning: to ... a rumour or plan is to stop it

explanation.surface: Stop making strong spirits.
explanation.definitionFit: To scotch is to put a stop to something, and Scotch is Scottish whisky, a strong spirit.

clue.text: Circular letter written by a dry fellow in prison accommodation

indicators.note: in puts the letter and the abstainer inside the word for a prison

parts.note: a cage confines like a prison
O is the round-shaped letter
TT stands for teetotal, one who drinks no alcohol

explanation.surface: A round-robin is penned by a teetotal inmate in his cell.
explanation.definitionFit: A cottage is a small house, a form of lodging.

clue.text: Anglican Church puts lieutenant in charge of European people

parts.note: CE is the Church of England, the Anglican church

explanation.surface: The church appoints an officer to lead a group of Europeans.
explanation.definitionFit: Celtic describes the Celts, an ancient people of western Europe.

clue.text: The proportion to turn traitor to a sacred cow

parts.note: to rat is to betray one's side
in Greek myth Io was turned into a heifer, a cow beloved of Zeus

explanation.surface: Someone betrays a cherished belief.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sacred cow' looks like an idiom for an unquestionable belief; here it is Io, the maiden Zeus turned into a heifer.
explanation.definitionFit: A ratio expresses the relative size of two quantities.

clue.text: Helooks at a periodical

explanation.surface: A man reads a magazine.
explanation.definitionFit: An onlooker watches an event, and The Spectator is a British weekly political magazine.

clue.text: Stolen goods returned along with small instruments

indicators.note: returned means the word for plunder is read backwards

parts.note: loot is plunder, stolen goods
S is the abbreviation for small, as on clothing sizes

explanation.surface: A thief hands back loot together with little gadgets.
explanation.definitionFit: Tools are instruments or implements used for work.

clue.text: Perhaps a stoic eccentric in the past

indicators.note: eccentric signals the words that follow are made odd, rearranged

explanation.surface: An odd philosopher from olden times.
explanation.walkthrough: The Stoic philosophers held that God and nature are one, so a stoic is an example of the believer described.
explanation.definitionFit: Stoic philosophy identified the divine with the universe, so a Stoic is an example of one who believes God is in everything.

clue.text: Greetings from Hawaii

parts.note: the word islanders use to say hello and goodbye

explanation.definitionFit: It is the Hawaiian word used as a salutation of welcome or farewell.

clue.text: Naive smile for the photographer in Stilton

parts.note: green means inexperienced or naive
people say cheese to make themselves smile for a photo

explanation.surface: An innocent grin for the camera, mouth full of English cheese.
explanation.walkthrough: STILTON is a blue-veined English cheese; mould gives it its greenish streaks.
explanation.definitionFit: Stilton is a blue-veined cheese whose mould can be greenish, so it is an example.
